:::{#exm-surprisal-chain-rule-noisy-copy}
#### Chain rule for surprisal with a noisy copy
<!-- no-figure: the example reports a handful of numbers, with nothing to plot -->

For the outcomes in @exm-joint-conditional-surprisal,
the surprisal of $x = 0$ plus the conditional surprisal of $y = 1$ given $x = 0$
is $`r round(s_x + s_y_given_x, 3)`$ bits.
It equals the joint surprisal $\surprisalf{0, 1} = `r round(s_xy, 3)`$ bits
(@thm-surprisal-chain-rule).
Subtracting $\surprisalf{0} = `r round(s_x, 3)`$ bit from the joint surprisal
recovers $\surprisalf{1 \mid 0} = `r round(s_xy - s_x, 3)`$ bits
(@cor-conditional-surprisal-difference).

:::
